Source: A 9-hour-old newborn girl is found in the newborn nursery with diffuse swelling of the scalp not present at birth.
On physical exam, she appears to be in mild distress and has a 4x5 cm ecchymotic area of swelling over the bilateral parietal bones.
The mother went into spontaneous labor but the delivery was complicated by a prolonged 2nd stage of labor.
The child was born at 38 weeks of gestation to a 28-year-old G3P3 mother.
Her temperature is 98.6°F (37°C), blood pressure is 67/43 mmHg, pulse is 135/min, and respirations are 34/min.
The pregnancy was complicated by preeclampsia in the mother which was well-controlled throughout the pregnancy.
Serial assessments of the child’s head circumference over the next 12 hours show no change in the size of the swelling.
The child’s Apgar scores were 8 and 9 at 1 and 5 minutes, respectively.
